references.text: Describes how kings and rulers gather against the Lord and His Anointed, parallel to how the Pharisees gathered against Jesus.
Enemies who set hidden traps resemble the Pharisees' plans to destroy Jesus.
Daniel in the lion's den refers to the innocent being persecuted, parallel to Jesus' situation.
The chief priests and elders gather to find a way to arrest and kill Jesus, directly parallel to the actions of the Pharisees.
The Pharisees went out and immediately began making plans with the Herodians on how they could kill Jesus, referring to the same event or similar thinking.
The anger and discussions among the Pharisees about what to do with Jesus resemble their planning in Matthew.
The leaders try to find a way to arrest Jesus but fear the crowd, parallel to the Pharisees' fear of the people's reaction.
The Jews begin to persecute Jesus and seek to kill him because he broke the Sabbath, parallel to the motives of the Pharisees.
From that day on they planned to kill him, referring to a similar conspiracy as in Matthew.
